title: Relief from Employer Benefit Charging Charges: Grounds and Limits
content:
Employer Benefit Charging allows an employer to be relieved of the benefit charges on a position only on the grounds its charge class allows.

## 1. The grounds

Relief from charges is granted only on a ground the employer's class allows:

- (a) the claimant left this employer voluntarily without good cause attributable to it;
- (b) this employer discharged the claimant for misconduct connected with the work;
- (c) the claimant refused suitable work this employer offered;
- (d) this employer still employs the claimant part time as in the base period;
- (e) the benefits were paid in error by the agency; or
- (f) the employer paid no base-period wages or the wages charged are wrong.

Which of these grounds a class allows is set per charge class.

## 2. Continuing part-time relief

Continuing part-time relief lasts only for weeks in which the employer keeps the claimant at the base-period average weekly hours, and ends from the first week the hours fall.

## 3. Reimbursing employers

Reimbursing employers are relieved only for continuing part-time employment, agency error and wrong wages, because they pay for benefits dollar for dollar.

## 4. Extended Benefits charges

Relief granted on the regular claim also covers the employer's Extended Benefits charges on the same claimant.

## 5. The pattern-of-failure bar on agency-error relief

Relief for benefits paid in error is refused when the employer's response to the notice of claim was untimely or inadequate and the employer's failed responses meet both the pattern count and the pattern rate. The failed responses are counted over the employer account's positions noticed in the lookback period before the overpayment determination date: the number whose response was late or never came, and that number divided by all positions noticed in the period. In every charge class the pattern count is 2, the pattern rate is 0.02 (2%) and the lookback is 365 calendar days.

| Response to this notice untimely or inadequate | Failed responses at least 2 | Failed share at least 2% | Agency-error relief |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Refused |
| Yes | Yes | No | Not refused by this bar |
| Yes | No | Yes | Not refused by this bar |
| No | Yes | Yes | Not refused by this bar |

## 6. Determinations on a response

A determination on the employer's response that grants relief moves the position to relieved; a determination that grants no relief leaves the position chargeable.

## 7. Effect of a granted relief

The clause "A granted relief credits back every charge already posted within its scope" is **no longer in force** for the relief credit of a protest decision or of a determination on a separation response, each of which is now fixed on its own basis. A relief that an appeal decision grants still credits the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope. No further charges are posted on a relieved position — that part of the rule remains in force.
